newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Koc won't sell Tofas stake to Fiat.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Koc won't sell Tofas stake to Fiat.

text.p: The head of Turkey's leading industrial group Koc Holding on Thursday ruled out the sale of its stake in top Turkish car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi to the venture's foreign partner Fiat Spa.

"Selling (to Fiat) is out of the question. Tofas is a company which has paid its dues. If necessary it will be closed tomorrow, but this business won't go as far as closure," Rahmi Koc was quoted as telling reporters by Anatolian news agency.

The comment came amid a growing row in Turkey between the government and the automotive industry over a duty free car import scheme which car and parts makers warn could undermine domestic manufacturers.

The scheme will allow Turkish residents and expatriates to import one foreign car under five years of age without import tax from June 1, 1997 if they deposit 50,000 marks for one year at public Ziraat bank for a year by end-1996.
Tofas has already acted to counter a sharp fall in demand prompted by expectations of cheaper car imports.
On Wednesday, Tofas put all its 4,500 workers on compulsory leave until next Tuesday after capacity usage fell below 40 percent at its Bursa plant.
The announcement followed a decision to cut production from two shifts to one next week and make 1,011 workers redundant from January.
The decree, which was originally limited to expatriates was recently extended to Turkish residents.
Koc on Thursday warned of more possible measures. "If there is a (further) decline in vehicle sales, we will consider what is necessary," he said in response to questions connected with the scheme.
Speaking at an International Chambers of Commerce (ICC) meeting in the southern Turkish city of Antalya, he added that the scheme would harm allied industries the most.

Turkey's State Minister Abdullah Gul said on Thursday that the scheme, devised as a source of badly needed state revenues, had so far raised $110 million, with applications to bring in 2,015 duty free cars.
Koc and Fiat each have a 37.86 percent stake in Tofas. The distributor and marketing firm Tofas Oto Ticaret is 37.5 percent owned by Fiat and Koc holds 28.45 percent.
Speculation that Fiat would buy Koc's Tofas stakes prompted strong gains in shares of Koc Holding and its automotive interests in October.
